title: Open and closed normalizations of the fixed extension model
statement: Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be one coefficient immersion [def-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-data], with fixed extension $F_a$ and restriction $r_a:a^*F_a\cong1$ [def-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-model]. If $a$ is open, there is an adjunction $F_a\dashv a^*$ whose unit satisfies $\eta_M;r_{a,M}=1_M$. If $a$ is closed, there is a natural isomorphism $e:F_a\cong a_*$ with $r_{a,M}=a^*(e_M);\varepsilon_{a,M}$ for the actual pullback/direct-image adjunction. No composition comparisons for pairs of immersions or higher coherence laws are asserted.

proof.text: The open-restriction-counit lemma gives $h^{-1}c_*\cong c_{W,*}h_S^{-1}$ for a closed $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ and an open $h:W\hookrightarrow V$, with $S_W=S\times_VW$, and gives compatibility with the actual closed counit. For opens $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $q:W\hookrightarrow X$, the extension presheaf restricted to $W$ is the extension presheaf for $U\times_XW\hookrightarrow W$: a test object over $W$ factors through $U$ precisely when it factors through the intersection. The unique summand and its sections agree, and otherwise both values are zero. Slice sheafification commutes with restriction; the module actions agree by the unique extension property of module sheafification. Hence $q^{-1}j_!\cong(U\times_XW\hookrightarrow W)_!(U\times_XW\to U)^{-1}$. This proves only open restriction calculations, not arbitrary closed base change.

proof.text: Pure open extensions compose canonically: for opens $h:W\hookrightarrow V$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$, $v_!h_!$ and $(vh)_!$ are both left adjoint to $h^{-1}v^{-1}\cong(vh)^{-1}$. Apply the unit-compatible-left-adjoint comparison to obtain $v_!h_!\cong(vh)_!$. All adjunctions here are open adjunctions; the comparison restricts to the identity on $W$, since its defining unit equation becomes the two open restriction identifications. Pure closed direct images compose by the evaluation formula $M(S\times_V(V\times_XE))\cong M(S\times_XE)$; the fibre-product associativity map is the identity after the canonical restriction identifications on $S$. Composition of open immersions is open from the definition, and composition of closed immersions is closed: on affine opens the two surjective ring maps compose to a surjection. These are the elementary geometric cases of Stacks Tag 02V0.

source.place: proof (2), pure open and pure closed composition; schemes.tex Tag 02V0 and proetale.tex Tags 09AA, 09BN

proof.text: Here is the shrinking argument for a closed factor. Let $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ be closed and $h:W\hookrightarrow V$ open containing the image of $S$; write $d:S\hookrightarrow W$ for its restriction. Apply the closed-subset realization theorem to $V\setminus W$, obtaining a closed immersion $e:D\hookrightarrow V$ with that image. Since $D$ is disjoint from $S$, its map to $V$ factors through the open $V\setminus S$. The cross-vanishing $(V\setminus S)^{-1}c_*=0$, followed by inverse-image composition, gives $e^{-1}c_*M=0$. The localization sequence for $h,e$ therefore identifies $h_!h^{-1}c_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}c_*M$. Step 3 identifies $h^{-1}c_*M=d_*M$. We have obtained a natural isomorphism $h_!d_*\cong c_*$ restricting to the identity on $S$: the open counit restricts to the inverse open unit by its triangle identity, and the closed restriction comparison is the counit of Step 1. In the actual identified-coefficient presentation, use the proved support criterion for the open counit in lem-sfb-proetale-identified-open-closed.

source.place: proof (2), factorization comparison by shrinking an ambient open

proof.text: For two factorizations $a=v c=v'c'$, use the open subscheme $W=V\times_XV'$ of $X$. Both maps from $S$ to $V,V'$ factor through $W$, and $d:S\hookrightarrow W$ is closed, being the restriction of $c$ (equivalently $c'$) to this open. Step 5 identifies $c_*\cong(W\hookrightarrow V)_!d_*$ and $c'_*\cong(W\hookrightarrow V')_!d_*$. Step 4 therefore identifies both extension functors with $(W\hookrightarrow X)_!d_*$. These are normalized isomorphisms: their restrictions to $S$, using $r_a$, are the identity. This proves factorization independence without a composite adjunction. Step 2 shows that the normalized comparison is unique, so comparisons via a further intersection agree and satisfy the cocycle law. The topology and scheme structure used here are literal open restrictions of the given closed immersions, not an inference that an arbitrary morphism factors through a closed subscheme merely from its image.
